metadata.description: Version of the plan in Partner Center. Keep the default.
Name of the managed resource group. Empty: mrg-m365permissions-<unique>.
Just-in-time access for support (automatic approval, 8 hours; change it on the application later). Only at install.
Marketplace: who gets the welcome mail (link and setup command) once the instance runs. Empty: none.
Display name of the scanned tenant (the instance reads it from Microsoft Graph when empty).
Plan size, chosen by number of users: the minimum, the plan never moves below it. Only B1 moves up by itself: it starts on B2 until the first scan is done, and goes to B2 while a scan backlog lasts.
Mailbox the scan identity may send alert mails as (set up in Exchange by the deployment script). Empty: none.

IP ranges (CIDR or single IPv4, comma separated) that may reach the web app; everything else is refused. Empty on a managed application: peered, public until the peering is up; not peered, nobody gets in. Elsewhere empty: open, protected by sign-in.
Marketplace: tags per resource type (Microsoft.Common.TagsByResource in the form), on top of tags.
Address space (CIDR, /20 to /25) of the instance's own virtual network. Empty: 10.250.0.0/24.

Resource id of the customer's virtual network, in any subscription of the tenant and any region. The worker peers with it once the setup command gave the scan identity Network Contributor on it, then closes the web app to the internet (on a managed application only without allowed IP ranges). Empty: no peering.

The customer reaches the web app through a private endpoint of their own, in any of their networks and subscriptions; no peering and no zone of the instance's. An Admin approves its connection in Settings, Access; public access then goes off (on a managed application only without allowed IP ranges). Ignored with peerVirtualNetworkId.

With peerVirtualNetworkId: the private IPv4 address of a firewall in that network. Once the peering is up the worker routes the apps' outbound traffic through it (Azure Resource Manager stays direct), tests sign-in and Microsoft Graph through it and goes back to direct traffic when they cannot be reached. An Admin changes it in Settings, Access. Empty: direct.

With peerVirtualNetworkId, instead of outboundFirewallIp: outbound traffic follows the routes that network advertises (its VPN or ExpressRoute gateway or Azure Route Server, 0.0.0.0/0). Once the peering is up the worker lets our link use that gateway (and the link of the customer allow gateway transit), keeps Azure Resource Manager direct, and goes back to direct traffic when no default route arrives or sign-in and Microsoft Graph cannot be reached. An Admin changes it in Settings, Access.

Resource id of the customer's own privatelink.azurewebsites.net private DNS zone (any subscription), for peering or ownPrivateEndpoint. The instance then makes no zone of its own; the setup command grants the scan identity Private DNS Zone Contributor on that zone only and the worker keeps the web app's two A records there. Empty: the instance's own zone (peering), or the customer's own DNS (ownPrivateEndpoint).
Storage and Key Vault through private endpoints (public access off, extra cost) instead of service endpoints.
